items.title: Elasmotherium at Dawn
items.caption: Late Pleistocene steppe: Elasmotherium, the giant 'Siberian unicorn' rhino, stands in frost-covered grass at sunrise, its breath steaming in the cold air. Accuracy note: the AI placed the horn toward the snout, whereas Elasmotherium's horn sat on its forehead.

items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Sabre-Tooth Above the Tar Seeps
items.caption: Late Pleistocene Rancho La Brea, about 20,000 years ago: a Smilodon fatalis rests on a sunlit rock above the glossy tar seeps of what is now Los Angeles, with oak and cypress woodland behind.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Irish Elk in the Morning Mist
items.caption: Late-glacial Ireland, about 13,000 years ago: a Megaloceros giganteus stag, the giant 'Irish elk', stands in a misty lakeside meadow of sedges and birch scrub in early autumn light. Accuracy note: the AI drew tall, narrow antlers; a real Irish elk's antlers spread very wide with broad flat palms, up to about 3.6 m across.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Ichthyosaurs Among the Ammonites
items.caption: Late Jurassic seas, about 160 million years ago: a pod of big-eyed Ophthalmosaurus ichthyosaurs hunts through a swirling school of ammonites in sunlit blue water. Accuracy note: the AI gave these Ophthalmosaurus rows of prominent teeth; the real animal had small, reduced teeth suited to soft prey like squid.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Arthropleura in the Coal Swamp
items.caption: Late Carboniferous coal-swamp forest, about 305 million years ago (Euramerica): a two-metre Arthropleura crawls over moss beneath Lepidodendron scale trees while a Meganeura griffinfly patrols overhead. Accuracy note: the body is rendered more domed than the flattened real animal, and the griffinfly looks smaller than its true 70 cm wingspan.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Pteranodon Colony on the Chalk Cliffs
items.caption: Late Cretaceous Kansas, Western Interior Seaway, about 85 million years ago: a Pteranodon longiceps nesting colony on chalky sea cliffs. Accuracy note: some animals have overly long, bird-like necks and a few flyers look tailed and bird-like; Pteranodon eggs were probably soft-shelled and buried, not left exposed in the open.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Glyptodons on the Pleistocene Pampas
items.caption: Late Pleistocene Argentine Pampas (~20,000 years ago): a pair of car-sized Glyptodon, armored relatives of armadillos, grazing at golden hour, with camelids and a lone Macrauchenia in the distance. Accuracy note: The shells show some armadillo-style banding, but a real Glyptodon carapace was one rigid dome of fused hexagonal plates. The tails are smoother than the real ringed, armored tails, and the distant Macrauchenia looks llama-like, without its trunk-like snout.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Coelacanths at the Reef Cave
items.caption: Two West Indian Ocean coelacanths (Latimeria chalumnae) at the mouth of a deep volcanic reef cave off the Comoros, about 200 meters down, in the present day. This lineage dates back about 400 million years and was thought to be extinct until 1938. Accuracy note: the AI made the white blotches denser and more mottled than the sparse spots on real coelacanths, and some fins look more ray-like than the real thick, fleshy lobes.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Paraceratherium at the Woodland Edge
items.caption: A herd of Paraceratherium, giant hornless rhinoceroses and among the largest land mammals ever, browses tall trees at the edge of an open woodland in Central Asia about 30 million years ago, during the Oligocene. Accuracy note: the AI gave the animals overly long, giraffe-like necks held nearly upright, while the real neck was shorter and thicker under a heavier head. The flat-topped trees also look more like modern African acacia savanna than Oligocene Asian woodland.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Spinosaurus in the Kem Kem River
items.caption: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus seizes a large Mawsonia, a coelacanth relative, while wading a muddy river in the Kem Kem system of North Africa, about 95 million years ago in the mid-Cretaceous. Accuracy note: the AI drew the sail as a rounded fan, but the real Spinosaurus sail was taller toward the middle of the back and more rectangular. The tail also lacks the tall, paddle-like fin that fossils show, and the snout is shorter and blunter than the real long, narrow one.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Dimetrodon at Dawn on the Permian Floodplain
items.caption: Dimetrodon, a sail-backed synapsid (closer to mammals than to dinosaurs), basks on a red mudbank of an Early Permian river floodplain in what is now north Texas, about 285 million years ago, while a second animal warms up across the channel. Accuracy note: the AI gave the sail a fan-like, frilled outline; the real sail was a skin membrane over separate long spines, with a more even curve. The head is too low and crocodile-like, missing Dimetrodon's tall, deep skull and big front teeth, and the palm-like trees look more modern than Permian seed ferns and conifers.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.

items.title: Cave Bears at the Den Mouth
items.caption: A cave bear (Ursus spelaeus) and her cub stand at the mouth of a limestone den above an alpine valley in Late Pleistocene Europe, about 40,000 years ago. Claw scratches mark the walls and old bones litter the floor, much like the real bear caves of the Alps. Accuracy note: the AI drew modern brown bears. Real cave bears were bulkier, with a high domed forehead, a steep brow and a shorter, broader face, and they ate mostly plants.
items.credit: AI-generated image (Grok Imagine). Artistic reconstruction, not a photograph.
